label: early original-phase o/i/p (and 2,g,q,u) after a w/s/e/t prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (97% of mass), mostly at positions 1-4 (t=2,3 carry ~67% of mass); never at t=0 or on the delimiter, and very rarely in the copy phase. The current input token matters most: o (7x lift), i, p, then 2, g, q, u. A prefix containing w (strongest), s, e, t, z or k makes it fire more often and harder. The top activations are o/i/p right after a run of w (e.g. w w [o], z w w w [p]). It prefers first occurrences of the token and sequences with few digits. It looks like a graded conjunction of current token and prefix rather than a crisp rule: o/i/p without a w/s/e/t prefix fire weakly or not at all, and the predicate has many false positives. Dev F1 0.40, mass recall 0.71.
